dsh-voice-mode port for the DSH 0.2 desktop app: streaming ASR into the draft, per-sentence TTS with
live captions, true barge-in, plus a local ASR correction dictionary.
# dsh-voice-mode-desktop
English | 中文
Full-duplex voice mode for **DeepSeek Harness 0.2 (desktop)**: speak and the words stream into the d
raft, pause and the message sends, the reply is read sentence by sentence, and speaking again interr
upts the read-aloud. Ships an in-app settings page for reading speed, input mode and captions.
This is an adapted fork of `dsh-voice-mode` 0.7.15 (which in turn derives from `haoku123/dsh-voice`)
. Both are MIT licensed; see LICENSE.
**What this fork is:** the compatibility adaptation that makes that plugin run on DSH 0.2 desktop —
it adapts the client API the plugin depends on, adds an in-app settings page, and replaces the cloud
read-aloud dependency with a small client kept inside this repository. The recognition, barge-in an
d local-TTS engines are upstream work, unchanged.

- Upstream declares compatibility up to DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 and is written against the 0.1 client API.
-
This fork targets DSH **0.2.0-rc.2** (the engine shipped with DSH NEXT desktop `2.0.17-next`), where
the client service `settingsScope` no longer exists and plugin settings forms only render `volatile

` fields.
- Verified on Windows, DSH NEXT desktop `2.0.17-next`, `@deepseek-ai/* 0.2.0-rc.2`. Other
versions are untested.
## What it does
- **Voice in**: press-and-hold or continuous listening, streaming recognition into an editable draft

, silence-based auto-send.
- **Voice out**: sentence-by-sentence read-aloud (Edge cloud TTS by defau

lt; local VITS / Kokoro optional), live captions.
- **Full duplex**: speaking while the reply is rea

d stops playback and cancels the running turn.
- **Settings page**: reading speed (0.5–2.0), input m
ode (hold / continuous), caption show-hide, and a one-click audio self-test. Reachable from the side
bar **Plugins** page as the item **语音模式 / Voice mode**. The self-test deliberately separates synthes
is from playback, so a silent reply can be traced to the engine or to the audio output instead of be
k, so a silent reply can be traced to the engine or to the audio output instead of being guessed at.
## One conversation, end to end

1. Hold the shortcut and speak; recognition streams into an editable draft.
2. Release to submit; th

e agent starts replying.
3. Replies are synthesized sentence by sentence while captions follow along

.
4. Speaking again during playback interrupts it immediately and starts the next turn.
5. One actio
n decides everything: releasing is what tells it you are done talking.
## How to use it: hold to speak
Day to day this plugin is meant to be used **hold-to-speak**: hold the shortcut, say one sentence, r
elease. In the voice session pick "hold" as the recording mode and "manual" as the barge-in mode.
**Full duplex (always listening + auto barge-in) is not the recommended everyday mode, and it has no
regression coverage.** The reason is practical: it hands the timing to the model. It may start acti
ng before you finish, or keep listening after you are done, and you lose control over when it stops
and when it acts. Hold-to-speak keeps both decisions with you: release means the sentence is finishe
d, and only then may it act.

- Want predictable control: hold-to-speak + manual barge-in (recommended).
- Trying full duplex: fin
e, but treat it as experimental. If it talks over you or fails to stop, switch back to hold-to-speak
before blaming the plugin.
## Test environment
All speed and resource numbers below come from this machine, not from synthetic or borrowed figures:

- CPU: Intel Core i5-14490F
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (8 GB VRAM)
- RAM: 32 GB
- OS: Windows
Different hardware scales the numbers; VRAM use depends on whether the GPU tier is loaded.

## Known limitations
- **Compiled artifacts**: `lib/` is upstream's built output with this fork's edits applied, not rege
nerated from source. Read the diff against `dsh-voice-mode@0.7.15` rather than expecting readable so

urce.
- **Cloud TTS by default**: `ttsEngine: edge` sends the spoken text to Microsoft. Use `vits` o

r `kokoro` for fully local synthesis.
- **Barge-in on speakers** depends on the browser's echo cance

llation; on Windows, hold-to-talk or headphones give the most reliable interruption.
- **Settings pe
rsistence** covers `rate` and `mode` (the two `volatile` fields). Other options are read from the pr

ofile patch at startup.
- **Diagnostics write to a local log**: to pin down "an entire utterance wen
t missing", the plugin writes every finalised segment (up to 400 characters) plus a set of pipeline
events into DSH's application log (`desktop-next.log`). The log stays on the machine and the diagnos
tics endpoint listens on loopback only (`POST /voice-mode/diag`, same-origin checked); its content,
however, is your own dictated text — clear the log periodically, and avoid installing this on a shar

ed account.
- **The correction dictionary is a local file**: entries live in `~/.dsh/voice-dict.json
` (override with the `DSH_VOICE_DICT` environment variable) and are not shipped with this package; t

he repository carries the matching logic only, never anyone's entries.
- **Full duplex has no automa
ted regression**: always-listening + auto barge-in depends on echo cancellation and endpointing, and
its timing varies with device and room. The checks in this repo only cover the hold-to-speak path;
full duplex gets manual smoke testing only, so verify it by hand when you touch that code.
## Compatibility matrix
| DSH (`@deepseek-ai/*`) | Desktop shell | Status |

| 0.2.0-rc.2 | DSH NEXT `2.0.17-next` (Windows) | verified (load, settings, TTS, recognition) |
| 0.

1.7-rc.1 and older | — | use upstream `dsh-voice-mode` |
| other | — | untested |
